note: Larkspur's teaching database: a generated orders table and a real B+tree, with page counts read off them. Round sizes chosen to show the mechanism, not any real database's numbers.

words.page: a table page holds 50 orders; an index page holds 50 keys
words.read: every page read costs the same, wherever it is
words.fetch: every row an index points to costs one page read to fetch
words.planner: the planner guesses each plan's pages from estimated rows and picks the cheaper: a stated rule, not any real database's planner
words.scale: the million-row counts are computed by formula from the 10,000 rows stored here
